reviewer_rationale: As of 2026-08-31, Solana's official fee-structure documentation states that 50% of the base transaction fee is burned (removed from circulating supply) and 50% goes to the block-producing validator. This meets VA_BURN because a live protocol rule irreversibly destroys a fixed share of the native token on every transaction; priority fees (100% to validator per SIMD-0096) are unrelated to this active burn rule.

As of 2026-08-31, the same documentation confirms the 50% base-fee burn is a live, automatic protocol rule applied to every transaction. This meets VA_PROTOCOL because usage-linked token burn is an explicitly qualifying value-capture route under the project definition, distinct from fees paid to validators as compensation.

As of 2026-08-31, Avalanche's official primary-network AVAX token documentation states that 'the fees used to execute a transaction on Avalanche is burned, or permanently removed from circulating supply,' while validators are instead compensated through newly minted staking rewards. This meets VA_BURN because 100% of transaction fees are irreversibly destroyed by a live protocol rule, with no fee revenue paid to validators.

This meets VA_PROTOCOL because the entire transaction fee is a usage-linked burn under a live protocol rule, an explicitly qualifying capture route, and is not paid to validators or miners as service compensation.

As of 2026-08-31, TRON's official economic-model documentation states that when an account's staked Bandwidth or Energy is insufficient, TRX is burned at fixed rates (0.001 TRX per byte of Bandwidth; 0.0001 TRX per unit of Energy) to cover the shortfall, permanently removing it from circulation. This meets VA_BURN because it is a live protocol rule that irreversibly destroys TRX tied to transaction resource consumption, though the same documentation notes stakers with sufficient frozen TRX pay no fee, so the burn is conditional on resource shortfall rather than universal.

This meets VA_PROTOCOL because the resource-shortfall burn is a usage-linked token-destruction route under a live protocol rule. Separately, the documentation shows block rewards (8 TRX/block to the producing Super Representative, 128 TRX/block distributed to voters) are funded by new issuance, not by fee revenue, so that reward stream does not itself support this classification -- the qualifying route here is specifically the burn.

As of 2026-08-31, the XRP Ledger's official documentation states that 'the transaction cost is not paid to any party: the XRP is irrevocably destroyed' on every transaction. This directly meets VA_BURN as a live, universal, automatic protocol-level burn.

This meets VA_PROTOCOL because the transaction-cost burn is a usage-linked, protocol-enforced token destruction on every transaction -- an explicitly qualifying capture route -- with the fee going to no validator or other service provider.

As of 2026-08-31, Cardano's official monetary-policy documentation states that fees from every transaction are collected into a virtual pot each epoch and then distributed -- 20% to the treasury, the remainder as staking rewards to pool operators and delegators. This does not meet VA_BURN because no portion of the fee is destroyed; the full fee amount is retained and redistributed within the protocol.

This does not meet VA_PROTOCOL because the fee pot is distributed as ordinary staking rewards to pool operators and their delegators, which is the standard proof-of-stake compensation mechanism the rule explicitly excludes ('do not infer capture merely because the token is used for... staking'); the 20% treasury share funds ecosystem governance rather than an evidenced automatic holder-capture route. Flag for discussion: whether the treasury allocation itself should be treated as a distinct 'governed protocol-revenue route' pending clarification of the project definition's scope for treasury-funded mechanisms.
